source_text: ἔσθ' ὅτε καὶ ἀργαλέαν ἐξανῦσαι, ὡς πειραθησόμενοι πλείονος εὐνοίας μὲν τῆς περὶ τὴν πρεσβείαν ἀπὸ ὑμῶν, μετουσίας δὲ τῆς τῶν φιλοτιμουμένων ὑπὲρ τοῦ εὖ ἀγαθῶν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ. ἐν γὰρ ταῖς ἁγίαις αὐτοῦ ἐκκλησίαις καὶ τοῖς εὐκτηρίοις καὶ μαρτυρίοις, ὡς ἐν ἄλλοις οὐρανοῖς, τὰ ἀνέκλειπτα αὐτοῦ προὔθηκεν ἀγαθά· καὶ ἀφ' ὧν οὗτος αὐτὸς ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων δέδωκέν τε καὶ ὁσημέραι δίδωσιν ἑκάστοις, ἀπὸ τούτων εὐσεβῶς καὶ ὁσίως προσφερομένην δέχεται ἀναίμακτον θυσίαν, καὶ πάντα ἔχει τὰ παρὰ ἀνθρώπων γέρα. νομίζω δὲ εἰς τὰ κατὰ αἱρετικῶν καὶ εἰς τὰ περὶ θεολογίας, καὶ τὰ ἄλογα ζῶα, μενοῦνγε τοὺς λίθους αὐτούς, τῇ προθυμίᾳ συμφθέγγεσθαι ἡμῖν. τί γὰρ οὐ ποιεῖ ὁ περὶ θεὸν ἔρως; ἢ τίνι παραχωρεῖ φίλτρον ἀληθὲς καρδίας; ἴστε γὰρ σὺν θεῷ δὲ πάντα εἰρήσθω οὕτω μεθ' ὑμῶν τε καὶ τῶν ἐκ τῆς ἡμετέρας φύσεως γεγονότων ἁγίων πρεσβευόντων πεπραχέναι, ὡς μηδένα πω μέχρι καὶ τήμερον οἷον δίκην τινά μοι καὶ κακηγορίας ἑλέσθαι λαχεῖν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν τῶν ἡμετέρων πρέσβεων τῶν τιμὰς τὰς πρὸς τὸ μέτρον ὑμῶν παρὰ πᾶσιν ἐχόντων· μηδὲ ὀνόματι καλέσαι με εἰς ἀγῶνα τὸν περὶ τούτου καὶ κρίσιν, καίτοι εὑρισκομένων τῶν τὰ μὴ ὄντα κατηγορούντων· ἀλλὰ μηδέ τινα πειραθῆναι διελέγξαι με ὡς εἴην λόγους ἀκούσας κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγου καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος καὶ δι' αἰδῶ τυχὸν ἢ φόβον τοῦ λέγοντος ἐπινεύσας καὶ τὰ μὴ καλὰ ἐπαινέσας· ἢ ὅλως ὀλιγωρήσας ποτὲ καὶ ἐν ῥαθυμίᾳ τῇ οὐκ ἐνδέοντι θέμενος τὸ πρὸς δύναμιν ἀντιτάξασθαι· μενοῦνγε ἐκ τοῦ ἐναντίου φάναι πολλούς, ὡς ἀεὶ παρῆλθον εὔτονος καὶ ἥμερος εἰς τὰ τοιαῦτα ἢ δώσων δίκην ἢ ληψόμενος. κέρδος γὰρ μέγιστον καὶ αἰώνιον ἐμαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν ἐξ ἐμοῦ καὶ τῶν σὺν ἡμῖν ἡγοῦμαι καλῶς τὸ πάντα πόνον, εἰ δεήσοι, καὶ κίνδυνον ἑλέσθαι ὑπὲρ τοῦ ποιήσαντος ἡμᾶς καὶ σώζοντος, καὶ κρῖναι καὶ φιλανθρωπεύσασθαι αὐτοῦ ἕνεκα ἔχοντος, πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ καὶ ἁγίου πνεύματος. εἰδότες οὖν, ὡς ἐκλεκτοὶ λατρευταὶ μὲν τῆς παναγοῦς τριάδος, πρεσβευταὶ δὲ τοῦ ἀνθρώπων γένους, μηδὲν μετ' αὐτὴν τὴν πάντων αἴτιον καὶ ζωοποιὸν αἰδοῦς εἰς ὑμᾶς ἐλλελεῖφθαί μοι τῆς ὀφειλομένης εἰς τοὺς συναγορεύοντάς με ταύτῃ τῇ χορηγούσῃ ἐνθυμήσεις καὶ φράσεις σοφὰς αὐτῇ τε
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: people travel to distant shrines, not shrinking from crossing a long sea, if need be, and a journey of many days in a row,] and sometimes even a hard one, to complete it, as people who are going to experience, on the one hand, greater goodwill concerning the intercession from you, and on the other, a sharing from God in the good things of those who strive zealously for the good. For in his holy churches and the houses of prayer and the martyrs' shrines, as in other heavens, he has set forth his unfailing good things; and from the things which this very King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule has given and daily gives to each, from these he receives a bloodless sacrifice offered piously and holily, and he has all the honours from men. And I think that in the matters against heretics and in the matters about theology, even the irrational animals, nay rather the stones themselves, join in uttering with us in eagerness. For what does the love toward God not do? Or to what does a true love of the heart give way? For you know, but let all things be said with God, that I have so acted, with you and with the saints who have come from our nature interceding, that no one yet, even up to today, has chosen to bring against me, as it were, some suit, even of slander, on behalf of you, our intercessors, who have honours suited to your measure among all; nor to call me by name into the contest and judgment about this, although those who accuse of things that are not are to be found; but not even that anyone tried to convict me as having heard words against God the Word and the Holy Spirit, and perhaps through respect or fear of the speaker having nodded assent and praised the things not good; or as having been at all negligent at some time and having placed in unfitting slackness the opposing according to my power; nay rather, on the contrary, that many say that I always came forward vigorous and gentle into such things, either to give satisfaction or to receive it. For I rightly consider it the greatest and eternal gain of myself and of those from me and of those with us to choose every toil, if it should be needed, and danger on behalf of the one who made us and saves us, and who is able to judge and to show loving-kindness on account of it, Father and Son and Holy Spirit. Knowing therefore, as chosen worshippers of the all-holy Trinity on the one hand, and intercessors of the race of men on the other, that nothing, after the very cause of all and life-giving [Trinity], has been left lacking by me of the reverence toward you, the reverence owed to those who plead with me to this [Trinity], the one supplying thoughts and wise phrases both to it [continues in the next section] ...
pass_b_english: …and at times a hard road at that, to see it through, as people who expect to find in you a greater goodwill toward their petition, and from God a share in the good things of those who strive eagerly for what is good. For in his holy churches, in the houses of prayer and the shrines of the martyrs, as in other heavens, he has set out his unfailing good things. And from the gifts that he himself, “the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule” (1 Timothy 6:15), has given and gives every day to each, from these he receives the bloodless sacrifice offered with piety and holiness, and he has every honour that men can give.

And I think that in the case against the heretics and in the things of theology even the brute beasts, nay rather the very stones, eagerly join their voices with ours. For what does love for God not do? Or to what does the heart’s true love give way?

For you know (but let all be said with God) that, with you and with the saints who came from our own nature interceding for me, I have so conducted myself that no one, even to this day, has yet chosen to bring against me any suit, so to speak, not even one for slander, on behalf of you, our intercessors, who receive from all people honours that match your measure. No one has summoned me by name to trial and judgment on this charge, though there are people to be found who accuse others of things that never happened. No one has even tried to convict me of having heard words spoken against God the Word and the Holy Spirit and then, perhaps from respect for the speaker or fear of him, of having nodded assent and praised what was not good; or of having ever been wholly negligent and treated with unbecoming slackness the duty of resisting as far as my strength allowed. On the contrary, many say that in such matters I always came forward vigorous and gentle, whether to answer for myself or to call others to account.

For I rightly count it the greatest gain, and an eternal one, for myself, for those who come from me and for those who are with us, to choose every toil, if need be, and every danger for the sake of him who made us and saves us, and who is able to judge, and to show loving-kindness on account of it: Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

Knowing, then, as chosen worshippers of the all-holy Trinity and intercessors for the human race, that after the Trinity itself, the cause of all and the giver of life, I have left nothing lacking in the reverence toward you that is owed to those who plead my cause with the Trinity, who supplies thoughts and wise words, both to itself…
notes: Khazarzar; Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify

lemmas.gloss: accomplish, see through to the end
strive eagerly, be zealous for honour
plead with, speak in support of

choices.issue: Garbled machine draft; address to the archangels lost; wrong reference
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u19): retranslated. The old English misread the opening ('they have even relaxed their efforts' for a journey 'sometimes even hard to complete'), εὐκτηρίοις as 'pleasant', συμφθέγγεσθαι as 'a readiness to agree', φίλτρον ... καρδίας as 'what true charm yields to the heart', παναγοῦς as 'all-encompassing', and turned the long legal period (no suit, no summons, no conviction) into a wish; the last period became 'I owe these wise reminders and phrases to her'. Reference: (Rev 19:16) -> (1 Timothy 6:15), since ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων is the wording of 1 Timothy, not of Revelation (βασιλεὺς βασιλέων).

choices.english: …and at times a hard road at that, to see it through
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence: the previous section ends καὶ πολλῶν ἐφεξῆς ἡμερῶν ὁδόν (a journey of many days in a row). Only the words this section holds are translated; 'road' renders the feminine ἀργαλέαν, which agrees with that ὁδόν.
The addressees are the archangels Michael and Gabriel, named in the previous section (ὦ εὐάρεστος ξυνωρὶς ἀρχαγγέλων), here joined with 'the saints who came from our own nature'.

choices.term: τῶν φιλοτιμουμένων ὑπὲρ τοῦ εὖ ἀγαθῶν
choices.english: the good things of those who strive eagerly for what is good
choices.why: φιλοτιμέομαι can also mean 'give generously', so the phrase may name the reward of generous givers; the more general sense is kept.

choices.term: ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων
choices.english: “the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule” (1 Timothy 6:15)
choices.why: Quoted in the wording of 1 Timothy 6:15; rendered literally so the participles stay visible.

choices.term: δίκην τινά μοι καὶ κακηγορίας ἑλέσθαι λαχεῖν
choices.english: to bring against me any suit, so to speak, not even one for slander
choices.why: δίκην λαγχάνειν τινί is the legal idiom 'bring a suit against someone'; κακηγορίας names the kind of suit. The infinitives (ἑλέσθαι, καλέσαι, πειραθῆναι, φάναι) all hang on ἴστε ('you know'), and are turned into separate English sentences.
θεὸς λόγος is this work's title for the Son (the previous section: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς λόγος οὐ διὰ τοὺς ἁμαρτήσαντας ἀγγέλους ἄγγελος).

choices.term: ἐν ῥαθυμίᾳ τῇ οὐκ ἐνδέοντι θέμενος τὸ πρὸς δύναμιν ἀντιτάξασθαι
choices.english: treated with unbecoming slackness the duty of resisting as far as my strength allowed
choices.why: τῇ οὐκ ἐνδέοντι does not agree with ῥαθυμίᾳ; it is read as οὐ δέον, 'improper'. Recorded in problems.

choices.english: whether to answer for myself or to call others to account
choices.why: δίκην διδόναι / λαμβάνειν: to submit to judgment or to exact it.
Kept as open as the Greek (family, household or disciples).

choices.term: κρῖναι καὶ φιλανθρωπεύσασθαι αὐτοῦ ἕνεκα ἔχοντος
choices.english: who is able to judge, and to show loving-kindness on account of it
choices.why: ἔχω with an infinitive = 'be able'. αὐτοῦ ἕνεκα is taken with the toil and danger just named (God judges and rewards because of them); 'for his own sake' is possible. Recorded in problems.

choices.term: τοὺς συναγορεύοντάς με ταύτῃ τῇ χορηγούσῃ
choices.english: those who plead my cause with the Trinity, who supplies
choices.why: ταύτῃ is the Trinity just named (τὴν πάντων αἴτιον καὶ ζωοποιόν); the dative is taken as the one before whom the archangels plead. 'The Trinity' is written out where the Greek has only the pronoun, because English needs the noun; no bracket.

choices.term: ἐνθυμήσεις καὶ φράσεις σοφὰς αὐτῇ τε
choices.english: thoughts and wise words, both to itself…
choices.why: The sentence runs into the next section (ἀρεσκούσας καὶ ἡμᾶς εὐεργετούσας, 'pleasing, and doing good to us'); only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.
